correction.behavior: Before registered detector calls, tokenize the exact candidate segment with the detector tokenizer and add_special_tokens=False. Compare the count against a per-family minimum derived from the pinned MarkLLM configs (KGW 2, Unigram 1, Unbiased 6, SynthID 5). If the count is below the family minimum, record each family/key detector test for that interval as applicability=invalid with reason zero_detector_tokens (count 0) or insufficient_detector_tokens (count 1..min-1) and do not call MarkLLM. Preserve the prior KGW min_prefix_len ValueError handling as defense-in-depth. All other exceptions re-raise.

root_cause: The prior zero-token precheck guarded only detector_token_count == 0. MarkLLM's Unbiased detector drops the final token before scoring (input_ids[..., :-1]), so a refined character interval that tokenizes to exactly one token reached Qwen2 with sequence length zero and failed during attention projection reshape. Intervals below a family-specific minimum must be treated as explicit detector non-applicability before any MarkLLM call, not only the zero-token case.
